verses.zh: 耶和华又向以色列人发怒，就激动大卫，使他吩咐人去数点以色列人和犹大人。
verses.en: The Lord’s anger again raged against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go count Israel and Judah.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The parallel text in 1 Chr 21:1 says, “An adversary opposed Israel, inciting David to count how many warriors Israel had.” The Samuel version gives an underlying theological perspective, while the Chronicler simply describes what happened from a human perspective. The adversary in 1 Chr 21:1 is likely a human enemy, probably a nearby nation whose hostility against Israel pressured David into numbering the people so he could assess his military strength. See the note at 1 Chr 21:1.
verses.commentary:
24:1 "the anger of the Lord" This chapter has several anthropomorphic phrases.

- the anger of YHWH, v. 1

- the hand of YHWH, vv. 14,17

- YHWH relented, v. 16

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE DEITY

▣ "number" There are two possibilities as to why this act was a sin.

- The people did not fulfill Exod. 30:12 (see Josephus, Antiq. 7.13.1).

- It was a faithless act on David's part failing to acknowledge that it was YHWH bringing the victory,
not the number of Israeli soldiers.

verses.zh: 大卫就吩咐跟随他的元帅约押说：「你去走遍以色列众支派，从但直到别是巴，数点百姓，我好知道他们的数目。」
verses.en: The king told Joab, the general in command of his army, “Go through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beer Sheba and muster the army, so I may know the size of the army.”

verses.zh: 约押对王说：「无论百姓多少，愿耶和华―你的　神再加增百倍，使我主我王亲眼得见。我主我王何必喜悦行这事呢？」
verses.en: Joab replied to the king, “May the Lord your God make the army a hundred times larger right before the eyes of my lord the king! But why does my master the king want to do this?”

verses.zh: 但王的命令胜过约押和众军长。约押和众军长就从王面前出去，数点以色列的百姓。
verses.en: But the king’s edict stood, despite the objections of[NOTE:1] Joab and the leaders of the army. So Joab and the leaders of the army left the king’s presence in order to muster the Israelite army.
notes: Heb “and the word of the king was stronger than.”

verses.zh: 他们过了约旦河，在迦得谷中、城的右边亚罗珥安营，与雅谢相对，
verses.en: They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, on the south side of the city, at[NOTE:1] the wadi of Gad, near Jazer.
notes: Heb “in the middle of.”
verses.commentary: 24:5-8 This geographical information is lacking in the 1 Chronicles 21 parallel.

verses.zh: 又到了基列和他停・合示地，又到了但・雅安，绕到西顿，
verses.en: Then they went on to Gilead and to the region of Tahtim Hodshi, coming to Dan Jaan and on around to Sidon.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

(חדשׁ, BDB 294, v. 18) and thereby the phrase is a time reference

(see NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 30).

verses.zh: 来到泰尔的保障，并希未人和迦南人的各城，又到犹大南方的别是巴。
verses.en: Then they went to the fortress of Tyre[NOTE:1] and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites. Then they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beer Sheba.
notes: For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.zh: 他们走遍全地，过了九个月零二十天，就回到耶路撒冷。
verses.en: They went through all the land and after nine months and twenty days came back to Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 约押将百姓的总数奏告于王：以色列拿刀的勇士有八十万；犹大有五十万。
verses.en: Joab reported the number of warriors[NOTE:1] to the king. In Israel there were 800,000 sword-wielding warriors, and in Judah there were 500,000 soldiers.
notes: Heb “and Joab gave the number of the numbering of the people.”
verses.commentary:
24:9 The numbers are very different between 2 Samuel 24 and 1 Chronicles 21. One wonders if a
different textual tradition is behind one of them. See note at v. 13.

verses.zh: 大卫数点百姓以后，就心中自责，祷告耶和华说：「我行这事大有罪了。耶和华啊，求你除掉仆人的罪孽，因我所行的甚是愚昧。」
verses.en: David felt guilty[NOTE:1] after he had numbered the army. David said to the Lord, “I have sinned greatly by doing this! Now, O Lord, please remove the guilt of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
notes: Heb “and the heart of David struck him.”

verses.zh: 大卫早晨起来，耶和华的话临到先知迦得，就是大卫的先见，说：
verses.en: When David got up the next morning, the Lord’s message had already come to the prophet Gad, David’s seer:

verses.zh: 「你去告诉大卫，说耶和华如此说：『我有三样灾，随你选择一样，我好降与你。』」
verses.en: “Go, tell David, ‘This is what the Lord has said: I am offering you three forms of judgment. Pick one of them and I will carry it out against you.’”

verses.zh: 于是迦得来见大卫，对他说：「你愿意国中有七年的饥荒呢？是在你敌人面前逃跑，被追赶三个月呢？是在你国中有三日的瘟疫呢？现在你要揣摩思想，我好回覆那差我来的。」
verses.en: Gad went to David and told him, “Shall seven[NOTE:1] years of famine come upon your land? Or shall you flee for three months from your enemies with them in hot pursuit? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now decide[NOTE:2] what I should tell the one who sent me.”
notes: The LXX has here “three” rather than “seven,” and is followed by NAB, NIV, NCV, NRSV, TEV, NLT. See 1 Chr 21:12.
Heb “now know and see.”
verses.commentary:
24:13 "seven years" The LXX and 1 Chr. 21:12 have "three years." This "three" may correspond to

- the three things of v. 12

- the three months of v. 13

- the three days of v. 13

The UBS Text Project, p. 286, gives the MT's "seven years" a "B" rating (some doubt).

The number differences can be caused by

- copyist's error

- different traditions of Hebrew texts

A new book that has helped me deal with these issues is John H. Walton and D. Brent Sandy, The Lost
World of Scripture, which deals with how oral cultures, such as the ANE, pass on their traditions. If these number issues
are a faith problem to you, please read this book.

When it comes to the number problems related to the reigns of kings, please consult Edwin R. Thiele,
The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings.

verses.zh: 大卫对迦得说：「我甚为难！我愿落在耶和华的手里，因为他有丰盛的怜悯。我不愿落在人的手里。」
verses.en: David said to Gad, “I am very upset! I prefer that we be attacked by the Lord, for his mercy is great; I do not want to be attacked by human hands!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “There is great distress to me. Let us fall into the hand of the Lord, for great is his mercy, but into the hand of man let me not fall.”
verses.commentary:
24:14 "but do not let me fall into the hand of man" It is possible that the "adversary" mentioned in 1 Chr. 21:1
was not "Satan" (there is no DEFINITE ARTICLE) but a close neighboring nation that David feared.

verses.zh: 于是，耶和华降瘟疫与以色列人，自早晨到所定的时候；从但直到别是巴，民间死了七万人。
verses.en: So the Lord sent a plague through Israel from the morning until the completion of the appointed time, and 70,000 people died from Dan to Beer Sheba.
verses.commentary:
24:15 "the appointed time" This probably refers to the time of the evening "continual," about 3 pm
(i.e., 1 Kgs. 18:29,36; Dan. 9:21; Acts 3:1).

verses.zh: 天使向耶路撒冷伸手要灭城的时候，耶和华后悔，就不降这灾了，吩咐灭民的天使说：「够了！住手吧！」那时耶和华的使者在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场那里。
verses.en: When the angel[NOTE:1] extended his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the Lord relented from his judgment.[NOTE:2] He told the angel who was killing the people, “That’s enough! Stop now!”[NOTE:3] (Now the angel of the Lord was near the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.)
notes: Heb “messenger.”
Heb “concerning the calamity.”
Heb “Now, drop your hand.”
verses.commentary:
24:16 "Araunah the Jebusite" The MT has האורנה

(the Qere form is ארונה, BDB 72, which most versions accept).

Jebusites were the Canaanite inhabitants of Jebus, later Jerusalem. The citadel was not captured
until David's reign.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

verses.zh: 大卫看见灭民的天使，就祷告耶和华说：「我犯了罪，行了恶；但这群羊做了甚么呢？愿你的手攻击我和我的父家。」
verses.en: When he saw the angel who was destroying the people, David said to the Lord, “Look, it is I who have sinned and done this evil thing! As for these sheep—what have they done? Attack me and my family.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “let your hand be against me and against the house of my father.”
verses.commentary:
24:17 "David saw the angel" As I read this chapter I wonder if this spiritual sight is connected to Joab's
words of v. 3, "while the eyes of my lord the king still see." Sin causes the sinner to not be able to perceive
the spiritual realm.

It is surely possible that v. 3 refers only to physical life!

verses.zh: 当日，迦得来见大卫，对他说：「你上去，在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场上为耶和华筑一座坛。」
verses.en: So Gad went to David that day and told him, “Go up and build an altar for the Lord on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”

verses.zh: 大卫就照着迦得奉耶和华名所说的话上去了。
verses.en: So David went up as Gad instructed him to do, according to the Lord’s instructions.

verses.zh: 亚劳拿观看，见王和他臣仆前来，就迎接出去，脸伏于地，向王下拜，
verses.en: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants approaching him, he[NOTE:1] went out and bowed to the king with his face[NOTE:2] to the ground.
notes: Heb “Araunah.” The name has been replaced in the translation by the pronoun (“he”) for stylistic reasons.
Heb “nostrils.”

verses.zh: 说：「我主我王为何来到仆人这里呢？」大卫说：「我要买你这禾场，为耶和华筑一座坛，使民间的瘟疫止住。」
verses.en: Araunah said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David replied, “To buy from you the threshing floor so I can build an altar for the Lord, so that the plague may be removed from the people.”

verses.zh: 亚劳拿对大卫说：「我主我王，你喜悦用甚么，就拿去献祭。看哪，这里有牛可以作燔祭，有打粮的器具和套牛的轭可以当柴烧。
verses.en: Araunah told David, “My lord the king may take whatever he wishes[NOTE:1] and offer it. Look! Here are oxen for burnt offerings, and threshing sledges[NOTE:2] and harnesses[NOTE:3] for wood.
notes: Heb “what is good in his eyes.”

Threshing sledges were heavy boards used in ancient times for loosening grain from husks. On the bottom sides of these boards sharp stones were embedded, and the boards were then dragged across the grain on a threshing floor by an ox or donkey.
Heb “the equipment of the oxen.”

verses.zh: 王啊，这一切，我亚劳拿都奉给你」；又对王说：「愿耶和华―你的　神悦纳你。」
verses.en: I, the servant of my lord[NOTE:1] the king, give it all to the king!” Araunah also told the king, “May the Lord your God show you favor!”
notes: The Hebrew text is difficult here. The translation reads עֶבֶד אֲדֹנִי (ʿeved ʾadoni, “the servant of my lord”) rather than the MT’s אֲרַוְנָה (ʾAravnah). In normal court etiquette a subject would not use his own name in this way, but would more likely refer to himself in the third person. The MT probably first sustained loss of עֶבֶד (ʿeved, “servant”), leading to confusion of the word for “my lord” with the name of the Jebusite referred to here.

verses.zh: 王对亚劳拿说：「不然。我必要按着价值向你买；我不肯用白得之物作燔祭献给耶和华―我的　神。」大卫就用五十舍客勒银子买了那禾场与牛。
verses.en: But the king said to Araunah, “No, I insist on buying it from you! I will not offer to the Lord my God burnt sacrifices that cost me nothing.”So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for 50 pieces of silver.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “50 shekels of silver.” This would have been about 20 ounces (568 grams) of silver by weight.

verses.zh: 大卫在那里为耶和华筑了一座坛，献燔祭和平安祭。如此，耶和华垂听国民所求的，瘟疫在以色列人中就止住了。
verses.en: Then David built an altar for the Lord there and offered burnt sacrifices and peace offerings. And the Lord accepted prayers for the land, and the plague was removed from Israel.

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 24:1-9

1Now again the anger of the Lord burned against Israel, and
it incited David against them to say, "Go, number Israel and Judah." 2The king said to Joab
the commander of the army who was with him, "Go about now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to
Beersheba, and register the people, that I may know the number of the people." 3But Joab
said to the king, "Now may the Lord your God add to the people a hundred
times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king still see; but why does my lord the king
delight in this thing?" 4Nevertheless, the king's word prevailed against Joab and against the
commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the
king to register the people of Israel. 5They crossed the Jordan and camped in Aroer, on the
right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad and toward Jazer. 6Then they
came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon,
7and came to the fortress of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and of the Canaanites,
and they went out to the south of Judah, to Beersheba. 8So when they had gone about
through the whole land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
9And Joab gave the number of the registration of the people to the king; and there were in
Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred
thousand men.
